annotations.description: Casting Amped Raptor into an opponent with an untapped Misty Rainforest (likely representing Daze or other interaction) is risky. More importantly, casting a creature before combat is generally suboptimal when holding tricks like Swords to Plowshares - though here there's nothing to attack with. The bigger question is whether Sand Scout would have been better: the opponent has an uncracked Misty Rainforest, so they likely have 1 land vs Sonnet Spike's 2, meaning Sand Scout's ETB would trigger to search for a Desert, providing ramp and setting up the token-generation ability. Amped Raptor's cascade-like ability is high variance and the energy may not find anything castable, while Sand Scout provides guaranteed value with the land advantage.

annotations.description: Casting Sand Scout before combat means the opponent sees the additional creature before blocks/combat decisions. With Ocelot Pride (lifelink) and Amped Raptor ready to attack, it would be better to attack first, then cast Sand Scout in second main phase. Attacking with Ocelot Pride could gain life (triggering its end-step token creation) and the opponent only has Misty Rainforest with no blockers visible. Additionally, casting creatures before combat when holding Swords to Plowshares (a combat trick of sorts) is generally suboptimal sequencing - you want to leave mana open and present fewer cards to the opponent's potential responses. However, Sand Scout's ETB ability to search for a Desert (opponent has 1 land, you have 3, so it won't trigger) makes pre-combat casting slightly less impactful. The main concern is giving information and not attacking first.

annotations.betterLine: Fetch Plains - covers the W-heavy hand while providing Wasteland protection. Already have sufficient color fixing from two Plateaus.

annotations.description: With Voice of Victory on the opponent's board ('Your opponents can't cast spells during your turn'), Haiku Valley needs to use their mana efficiently on their own turn. The opponent has Ocelot Pride (1/1 with lifelink) which will create tokens at end step if it gains life - meaning if it attacks and connects, it snowballs. Lightning Bolt on Ocelot Pride is the highest-impact play here, preventing the token generation engine from getting out of control. Brainstorm is a strong card but doesn't address the board pressure - the opponent already has Sand Scout, Voice of Victory, Amped Raptor, Ocelot Pride, and a Sand Warrior token. Additionally, Brainstorm could have been cast on the opponent's turn (Voice of Victory only prevents casting during opponent's turn, not your own turn... wait, actually Voice says 'Your opponents can't cast spells during your turn' - so Haiku Valley can't cast on Sonnet Spike's turn). Still, Lightning Bolt removing Ocelot Pride before it can attack and generate tokens is more urgent than card selection. The DRC surveil trigger happens either way.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Brainstorm for card selection
annotations.betterLine: Cast Lightning Bolt targeting Ocelot Pride to prevent the lifelink/token generation engine from snowballing. Brainstorm could be cast later, while Ocelot Pride gets more dangerous each turn it survives.

annotations.description: Cracking Misty Rainforest before Brainstorm resolves wastes the key Brainstorm+fetchland synergy. The fetch shuffle should happen AFTER Brainstorm resolves to shuffle away the two worst cards put back on top.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Misty Rainforest in response to their own Brainstorm (before it resolves)
annotations.betterLine: Let Brainstorm resolve first, draw 3 cards, put the 2 worst cards back on top, THEN crack Misty Rainforest to shuffle those cards away. This is the fundamental Brainstorm+fetch interaction in Legacy.

annotations.description: Playing Scalding Tarn instead of Volcanic Island when holding Ponder in hand. Volcanic Island provides the same mana immediately without costing life, and saving the fetchland allows shuffling after a future Ponder for better card selection. Additionally, Volcanic Island untapped gives access to both U and R mana right away.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Scalding Tarn from hand
annotations.betterLine: Play Volcanic Island from hand to preserve the fetchland for post-Ponder shuffle value and avoid paying 1 life when fetching

annotations.description: Skipped the attack phase entirely with a dominant board (Amped Raptor, Ocelot Pride, Sand Scout, Voice of Victory with Mobilize 2, Sand Warrior token) against only a single Dragon's Rage Channeler. Voice of Victory prevents the opponent from casting spells during Sonnet Spike's turn, meaning no combat tricks, no Daze, no Lightning Bolt. Attacking would deal massive damage (potentially 7+ with Mobilize warriors) and Ocelot Pride's lifelink would trigger end-step token creation.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast a spell (likely Staff of the Storyteller or similar) and skipped the attack phase entirely
annotations.betterLine: Attack with all or most creatures. Voice of Victory's Mobilize 2 creates two additional attackers, and its static ability prevents opponent from casting spells. DRC can only block one creature, allowing 7+ damage through. Ocelot Pride's lifelink triggers end-step token generation. Could cast spells post-combat.

annotations.description: Amped Raptor is just a 2/1 body that has already used its ETB ability. Ocelot Pride is an engine piece with lifelink that creates tokens at end step whenever life is gained, and with Voice of Victory's Mobilize creating tokens, this can snowball. Killing the engine piece is far more impactful than removing a vanilla 2/1 first striker.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted Amped Raptor with Lightning Bolt
annotations.betterLine: Target Ocelot Pride with Lightning Bolt to shut down the token generation engine before it snowballs

annotations.description: Lightning Bolt is on the stack likely targeting Dragon's Rage Channeler, Haiku Valley's only creature and key card for card selection/delirium strategy. Haiku Valley declined to counter it with Daze despite having two copies in hand.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority letting Lightning Bolt resolve without using Daze to counter it
annotations.betterLine: Cast Daze (returning Volcanic Island to hand) to counter Lightning Bolt and protect Dragon's Rage Channeler, preserving the primary threat on board

annotations.description: Declined to Swords to Plowshares a 3/3 Dragon's Rage Channeler that's attacking unblocked, taking 3 damage unnecessarily. With a dominant board (Ocelot Pride, Voice of Victory, Sand Scout, Sand Warrior token) and the opponent having very limited resources, removing their only creature now would effectively lock the game. DRC with surveil also helps the opponent dig for answers.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without casting Swords to Plowshares, taking 3 damage from DRC
annotations.betterLine: Cast Swords to Plowshares on Dragon's Rage Channeler to eliminate the opponent's only threat while having an overwhelming board advantage, effectively ending the game

annotations.description: Playing Volcanic Island directly into opponent's untapped Wasteland is risky. Misty Rainforest would be safer as it can be cracked in response to Wasteland, still providing access to blue/red mana while protecting the dual land for later.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Volcanic Island as land drop, exposing it to opponent's Wasteland
annotations.betterLine: Play Misty Rainforest instead - it's immune to Wasteland and can fetch Volcanic Island when mana is actually needed, preserving the dual land for a safer moment

annotations.description: With Ponder's ordering, Force of Will was chosen first meaning it goes to the bottom of the three cards, so it won't be drawn. Given the opponent's threatening board (Ocelot Pride, Voice of Victory, Sand Scout with token) and Voice of Victory preventing spells during opponent's turn, Force of Will is the most impactful card to draw immediately - it's the premier answer/protection spell and having it in hand is critical for surviving.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose Force of Will first in the Ponder ordering, placing it at the bottom (not drawn)
annotations.betterLine: Should have chosen Force of Will last so it ends up on top and is drawn by Ponder, giving immediate access to the most powerful card among the three options.

annotations.description: Haiku Valley wanted Brainstorm on top but misunderstood the ordering interface ('last one chosen will be topmost'). By selecting Brainstorm first, Wasteland ended up on top instead. With two untapped fetchlands available (Misty Rainforest, Scalding Tarn), Brainstorm would have been significantly more powerful as the next draw - allowing card selection and using fetchlands to shuffle away unwanted cards. Wasteland destroying one of three Plateaus is less impactful.
annotations.actionTaken: Put Wasteland on top of library (by selecting Brainstorm first in the ordering)
annotations.betterLine: Put Brainstorm on top of library (by selecting Wasteland first, then Brainstorm as the topmost card) to leverage the fetchland-Brainstorm synergy for better card selection

annotations.description: With 4 mana available (3 Plateaus + Wasteland), Sonnet Spike only cast Goblin Bombardment (1R), leaving 2 mana unused when they had multiple excellent 2-drops in hand. Hexing Squelcher would provide uncounterability for future spells and ward for all creatures against a blue deck, and could have been cast alongside Goblin Bombardment.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast only Goblin Bombardment, leaving 2 mana unused
annotations.betterLine: Cast Goblin Bombardment (1R) AND Hexing Squelcher (1R) to maximize board development and gain spell uncounterability against the blue opponent

annotations.description: Declined to chump block Dragon's Rage Channeler (3/3 with delirium) with a 1/1 token. Taking 3 damage (17→14) when the opponent likely has access to burn spells makes life total relevant. A 1/1 token is generally worth less than 3 life points.
annotations.actionTaken: Did not assign any blockers, taking 3 damage from Dragon's Rage Channeler
annotations.betterLine: Chump block with one of the 1/1 tokens (Cat or Warrior) to save 3 life. The token's combat/board value is likely less than 3 life against a UR deck with burn potential.

annotations.description: Ocelot Pride is the key engine generating exponential token advantage each end step when life is gained (it has lifelink). Killing Sand Scout removes a 2/2 body and its land-graveyard trigger, but Ocelot Pride will snowball the board with tokens every turn it attacks and connects. With Voice of Victory creating attacking warriors, the board is already spiraling.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted Sand Scout with Lightning Bolt
annotations.betterLine: Target Ocelot Pride with Lightning Bolt to kill the token-generating engine before it snowballs further

annotations.description: Haiku Valley cast Brainstorm in response to their own Lightning Bolt on the stack, spending mana and a card reactively when there was no pressing need. While Brainstorm is a good card, casting it here before resolving the Lightning Bolt doesn't accomplish much strategically - the Lightning Bolt was already on the stack targeting Sonnet Spike's board/life. More importantly, Brainstorm without a subsequent shuffle (fetchland crack) is less valuable, and they could have saved it for a more critical moment or cast it at end of turn with fetch shuffle available. The Brainstorm could have been saved to be cast alongside a fetchland crack for maximum value, rather than using it mid-stack where it doesn't change the combat math or protect anything.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Brainstorm in response to their own Lightning Bolt on the stack
annotations.betterLine: Let Lightning Bolt resolve first, then cast Brainstorm on Sonnet Spike's end step with fetchland available to shuffle away unwanted cards

annotations.description: Put Murktide Regent back with Brainstorm despite it being castable next turn for just UU with 7+ cards in graveyard for delve. With fetchlands available to shuffle, the put-back cards get shuffled away anyway, making it better to keep Murktide in hand where it's guaranteed accessible.
annotations.actionTaken: Put Murktide Regent on top of library with Brainstorm
annotations.betterLine: Keep Murktide Regent in hand and put back less impactful cards like Stormchaser's Talent or a second Daze, then fetch to shuffle away the put-backs. Murktide could be deployed next turn as a large flying threat.
